title: Experiment: ingress/egress token split with minimum monthly credit option
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Customers have asked for clearer cost signals for short prompt-heavy workloads (high input ratio) vs. long-generation streaming workloads (high output ratio). Our current uni-rate per-token billing obscures workload economics and can produce surprising bills for customers that heavily stream. Hypothesis: Offering a split rate (ingress vs egress tokens) combined with an optional minimum monthly credit package will (1) better align incentives for efficient prompting, (2) reduce billing surprise for streaming-heavy customers, and (3) increase predictable revenue via optional committed credits. Scope: This ticket designs and runs a controlled experiment for hosted API customers to validate pricing sensitivity and operational impacts. The plan covers rate matrix, commit credit SKUs, quota enforcement, reporting updates, and SRE/billing integration for reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment variants implemented in billing pipeline and metering layer for a subset of new signups and opt-in existing accounts
Analytics dashboard shows per-variant averages for ARPU, median bill delta, churn intent, and cost-to-serve within 14 days
No regressions in latency or rejected requests due to metering changes; SRE signoff on rollout runbook
Legal and finance approve commit credit terms and refund/carry-forward rules
Decision recommended: Roll forward (formal pricing), iterate (rework rates/commits), or roll back
metrics: Delta in average invoice amount (variant vs control) — mean and median
% of customers who opt into commit credits
Change in token mix (input vs output) per customer
Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) uplift from committed plans
Charge dispute rate / billing support tickets per 1k accounts
90th percentile request latency for metered requests (ensure < baseline + 5ms)
implementation_notes: Variant A: ingress rate = $0.000004 / token, egress rate = $0.000012 / token; no minimum
Variant B: same split rates with optional commit credit bundle (100k credits for $X with 1.25x top-up value) and soft monthly floor of 5k credits for committed accounts
Metering: add ingress/egress counters to existing usage pipeline; tag records with experiment_key=PM-13521
Billing pipeline: apply per-variant multipliers upstream of invoicing; implement commit SKU that deducts from egress-first consumption
Quota/limits: ensure quick-fail path unchanged; streaming sessions still enforce token-per-second SLOs
Billing UI: add banner and opt-in checkbox for eligible accounts; show simulated month cost under new split rates
Instrumentation: create dashboards (Looker/BigQuery) with cohort slicing by workload type (prompt-heavy vs stream-heavy)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers misunderstand ingress vs egress; mitigation: explicit examples, pricing calculator, and dedicated support doc
Risk: Integration with existing enterprise commit contracts (legal) may conflict; mitigation: include finance in definition, draft addendum templates
Risk: Metering miscount on streaming edge cases (partial chunks); mitigation: add end-to-end tests and reconciliation runbook
Risk: Increased billing disputes; mitigation: pilot with small cohort and hold refund reserve, monitor support queue closely
Risk: SRE overhead from tags in ingestion pipeline; mitigation: rate-limit pilot and provide rollback toggle
